import Mathlib

def total_weight (selected : List Bool) (weights : List Nat) : Nat :=
  match selected, weights with
  | [], _ => 0
  | _, [] => 0
  | b :: bs, w :: ws => (if b then w else 0) + total_weight bs ws

def total_value (selected : List Bool) (values : List Nat) : Nat :=
  match selected, values with
  | [], _ => 0
  | _, [] => 0
  | b :: bs, v :: vs => (if b then v else 0) + total_value bs vs

def is_valid_strategy (selected : List Bool) (weights : List Nat) (capacity : Nat) : Prop :=
  selected.length = weights.length ∧
  total_weight selected weights ≤ capacity

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def knapsack_01_precond (weights values : List Nat) (capacity : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  weights.length = values.length
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def knap : List Nat → List Nat → Nat → Nat
  | [], _, _ => 0
  | _ :: _, [], _ => 0
  | w :: ws, v :: vs, cap =>
      max (knap ws vs cap) (if w ≤ cap then v + knap ws vs (cap - w) else 0)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def knapsack_01 (weights values : List Nat) (capacity : Nat)
    (h_precond : knapsack_01_precond weights values capacity) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  knap weights values capacity
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def knapsack_01_postcond (weights values : List Nat) (capacity : Nat) (result : Nat)
    (_ : knapsack_01_precond weights values capacity) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ selected, is_valid_strategy selected weights capacity → total_value selected values ≤ result) ∧
  (∃ selected, is_valid_strategy selected weights capacity ∧ total_value selected values = result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem knap_ub (ws : List Nat) : ∀ (vs : List Nat) (cap : Nat) (sel : List Bool),
    sel.length = ws.length → ws.length = vs.length →
    total_weight sel ws ≤ cap → total_value sel vs ≤ knap ws vs cap := by
  induction ws with
  | nil =>
    intro vs cap sel hl _ _
    match sel with
    | [] => simp [total_value, knap]
    | b :: s => simp at hl
  | cons w ws ih =>
    intro vs cap sel hl hlen hw
    match vs, sel with
    | [], _ => simp at hlen
    | v :: vs, [] => simp at hl
    | v :: vs, b :: sel =>
      have hl' : sel.length = ws.length := by simpa using hl
      have hlen' : ws.length = vs.length := by simpa using hlen
      cases b with
      | false =>
        have hw' : total_weight sel ws ≤ cap := by simpa [total_weight] using hw
        have := ih vs cap sel hl' hlen' hw'
        simp only [total_value, knap, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, Nat.zero_add]
        exact le_trans this (le_max_left _ _)
      | true =>
        have hw' : w + total_weight sel ws ≤ cap := by simpa [total_weight] using hw
        have hc : w ≤ cap := by omega
        have hw2 : total_weight sel ws ≤ cap - w := by omega
        have := ih vs (cap - w) sel hl' hlen' hw2
        simp only [total_value, knap, if_true, hc]
        have : v + total_value sel vs ≤ v + knap ws vs (cap - w) := by omega
        exact le_trans this (le_max_right _ _)

theorem knap_ex (ws : List Nat) : ∀ (vs : List Nat) (cap : Nat),
    ws.length = vs.length →
    ∃ sel : List Bool, sel.length = ws.length ∧ total_weight sel ws ≤ cap ∧
      total_value sel vs = knap ws vs cap := by
  induction ws with
  | nil =>
    intro vs cap _
    exact ⟨[], by simp, by simp [total_weight], by simp [total_value, knap]⟩
  | cons w ws ih =>
    intro vs cap hlen
    match vs with
    | [] => simp at hlen
    | v :: vs =>
      have hlen' : ws.length = vs.length := by simpa using hlen
      obtain ⟨s1, h1l, h1w, h1v⟩ := ih vs cap hlen'
      by_cases hc : w ≤ cap
      · obtain ⟨s2, h2l, h2w, h2v⟩ := ih vs (cap - w) hlen'
        rcases le_total (v + knap ws vs (cap - w)) (knap ws vs cap) with h | h
        · refine ⟨false :: s1, by simp [h1l], ?_, ?_⟩
          · simpa [total_weight] using h1w
          · simp only [total_value, knap, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, Nat.zero_add, hc, if_true]
            omega
        · refine ⟨true :: s2, by simp [h2l], ?_, ?_⟩
          · simp only [total_weight, if_true]
            omega
          · simp only [total_value, knap, if_true, hc]
            omega
      · refine ⟨false :: s1, by simp [h1l], ?_, ?_⟩
        · simpa [total_weight] using h1w
        · simp only [total_value, knap, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, Nat.zero_add, hc, if_false]
          omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem knapsack_01_postcond_satisfied (weights values : List Nat) (capacity : Nat)
    (h_precond : knapsack_01_precond weights values capacity) :
    knapsack_01_postcond weights values capacity (knapsack_01 weights values capacity h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  constructor
  · intro sel hsel
    exact knap_ub weights values capacity sel hsel.1 h_precond hsel.2
  · obtain ⟨sel, hl, hw, hv⟩ := knap_ex weights values capacity h_precond
    exact ⟨sel, ⟨hl, hw⟩, hv⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Compiles clean on the first check — `LEAN VERIFIED` (only two unused-variable linter warnings, both from the pre-existing signatures).

**Approach:**

- **auxcode** — `knap`, the standard recursive 0/1 knapsack:
  ```
  knap (w::ws) (v::vs) cap = max (knap ws vs cap) (if w ≤ cap then v + knap ws vs (cap-w) else 0)
  ```
  Structural recursion on the lists, so no termination obligation.

- **code** — `knapsack_01 = knap weights values capacity`.

- **lemma** — two inductions on `weights`, generalizing over values, capacity (essential, since the "take" branch recurses at `cap - w`) and the selection:
  - `knap_ub`: any selection of matching length with weight ≤ cap has value ≤ `knap`. Split on the head bit: `false` bounds via `le_max_left`; `true` gives `w ≤ cap` and `total_weight sel ws ≤ cap - w` by `omega`, then `le_max_right`.
  - `knap_ex`: builds a witness achieving `knap` exactly. Case on `w ≤ cap` and on which side of the `max` wins, prefixing `false` (reuse the cap-witness) or `true` (reuse the `cap - w` witness).

- **proof** — the postcondition is exactly these two lemmas; `is_valid_strategy` destructs into the length and weight hypotheses, and the precondition supplies `weights.length = values.length`.

No `sorry`, `axiom`, `partial`, or other escape hatches; only the four marker regions were edited.
